topicCandidates: A duty-first comparison of Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, Instructor, Professor, Researcher, and Intra-company Transferee rather than selection by English job title.

Common job-title maps for technical work, humanities work, international services, English and other language teaching, academic teaching, research, and intra-group assignments, with each title presented as an example rather than a whitelist.

The English-teaching decision path: university or equivalent higher education, covered elementary or secondary education, qualifying vocational or miscellaneous-category schools, private language companies, international schools, preschools, direct-hire and dispatched ALT arrangements, and freelance or multi-employer instruction.

Engineer/Specialist qualification alternatives: relevant university or qualifying Japanese professional-training education, relevant experience, the international-services experience route, graduate exceptions for specified language work, recognized information-processing examinations, remuneration parity, and a qualifying Japanese contract.

The relationship between the applicant's field of study and actual duties, including the different treatment of university and Japanese professional-training education and the danger of relying on a degree title alone.

Mixed and incidental work: onboarding, practical training, customer contact, physical work, management, translation, sales, and administrative tasks that may be compatible only when subordinate to the qualifying principal activity.

Institution boundaries among Professor, Instructor, and Researcher, including university research, private or government research institutes, research guidance, non-degree appointments, part-time appointments, and work across multiple organizations.

Intra-company Transferee requirements: qualifying overseas and Japanese offices, a time-limited transfer, the required prior overseas service, covered professional duties, remuneration, corporate relationships, and the consequences of changing to an unrelated employer.
Available periods of stay, extension review, employer or institution changes, resident and organization notifications, outside-activity permission, and when a change of status may be needed.

Employer-side lawful recruitment, residence-card and work-authority checks, truthful duty design, written employment conditions, organization evidence, authorized COE representation, onboarding, employment reporting, and change or separation handling.

The distinct roles of the employer, applicant, Immigration Services Agency, diplomatic mission, and any licensed representative; an employer can support an application but cannot issue or guarantee a COE, visa, landing permission, or extension.
userSituations: A prospective English teacher comparing an ALT role, an eikaiwa position, an international-school job, and a university lecturer appointment without knowing that institution and duties can point to different statuses.
An ALT employed directly by a board of education or school versus an ALT dispatched by a private company to work at covered schools.
A language instructor teaching adults for a private conversation school whose role may sit under Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services rather than Instructor.
A university English lecturer, assistant professor, or researcher whose employment title does not itself establish whether Professor applies.

A preschool, kindergarten, after-school, tutoring, or international-school teacher who needs the institution's legal classification and real duties checked rather than being routed by the word teacher.
A software developer, software engineer, programmer, systems engineer, data professional, or IT consultant comparing degree, experience, and recognized-examination pathways.

A designer, translator, interpreter, marketer, sales-planning professional, accountant, consultant, or human-resources professional whose ordinary title conceals materially different duty and qualification questions.

An engineer whose role includes initial factory-floor training, installation, maintenance, customer support, or manual production work and needs the principal-versus-incidental activity boundary explained.
A corporate or government-laboratory researcher deciding between Researcher, Professor, Engineer/Specialist, Highly Skilled Professional, or a designated research program.

An employee transferred from an overseas affiliate to Japan who has the right professional duties but may not satisfy the corporate-relationship, prior-service, workplace, or limited-transfer conditions.

A foreign employer hiring its first international professional and trying to understand COE support, document responsibility, employment law, reporting, and onboarding without an internal immigration team.
A current work-status holder changing employers, adding freelance work, teaching for another institution, or combining roles across categories.
edgeCasesAndExceptions: English teacher is not a status category. University teaching can point to Professor, qualifying school teaching to Instructor, and private-company language teaching to Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services; edge institutions require classification rather than guesswork.
ALT is also not determinative. Direct employment, dispatch arrangements, the contracting organization, actual school and workplace, and assigned activities all need to be represented.

A job at an international school, preschool, kindergarten, cram school, after-school program, online platform, or employer training department cannot be classified safely from its English marketing label.
A bachelor's degree is not a universal stand-alone rule for every professional route, and a degree unrelated to the duties may require a different qualification pathway or closer evidence.

A university graduate performing translation, interpretation, or language instruction may fall within a stated international-services exception, but that exception should not be generalized to every foreign-culture role.
Recognized information-processing examinations can create a route separate from ordinary degree or experience evidence; an arbitrary commercial IT certificate does not necessarily qualify.
Software developer, systems engineer, data analyst, product manager, sales engineer, and consultant are useful discovery terms but remain too broad to establish status fit without a duty breakdown.

Routine customer service, retail, food service, factory-line, warehouse, cleaning, driving, and primarily manual work do not become professional activity merely because the title includes engineer, coordinator, manager, or international.
Practical training may be acceptable when temporary and connected to later qualifying duties, but indefinite assignment to non-qualifying work must not be normalized as onboarding.

Professor depends on activity at a university, equivalent institution, or college of technology; rank labels such as lecturer, assistant professor, visiting faculty, or researcher do not decide the status by themselves.

Researcher excludes activity within the Professor category. A role combining product development and original research may require classification by its principal duties and host rather than the word researcher.

Intra-company Transferee covers the same activity field as Engineer/Specialist but adds a qualifying group relationship, prior overseas service, a defined transfer period, and work at the relevant Japanese office.

A new external hire, a transfer after insufficient qualifying overseas service, or a move to an unrelated Japanese employer is not preserved as Intra-company Transferee merely because the company calls it an assignment.
Part-time or multiple appointments can alter evidence and notification needs. A Professor teaching for a private company is an official example of work that may require outside-activity permission.

The optional Certificate of Authorized Employment can help clarify permitted work but neither grants a status nor may be demanded where work authorization is otherwise clear as a condition for avoiding discriminatory treatment.

The resident's organization-change notification, an employer's foreign-worker employment notification, and any organization-side ISA notification are distinct; completing one does not prove that another duty or the new work-status fit has been resolved.
All five statuses currently list five years, three years, one year, or three months as available periods, but the period actually granted and any later extension remain individual decisions.

A COE or successful prior extension does not guarantee the next visa, landing, change, or extension decision, particularly after duties, organization, remuneration, finances, or compliance facts change.
jurisdictionVariables: National immigration statutes, landing criteria, ministerial notices, Immigration Services Agency guidance, and current application checklists.
The legal classification and facilities of the employing school, university, research institute, company, Japanese office, and overseas affiliate.
The applicant's exact contract, work locations, principal and incidental duties, remuneration, education, experience, examinations, and prior service.

Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare employment rules, written working-condition duties, foreign-worker employment reporting, social insurance, and workplace protections, which remain separate from immigration approval.
Professional licensing or regulated-activity law where a job includes reserved services, even if some surrounding work could fit a professional residence status.
Municipal onboarding and resident procedures after arrival, which employers may support but do not control.
The responsible Japanese diplomatic mission for the visa application and any nationality- or jurisdiction-specific supporting documents.
Individual ISA examination and regional procedure; local filing practice must not be represented as a different national activity definition.

contentImpacts.reason: Give the popular English-teaching entrance path a concise institution-first comparison across Professor, Instructor, Engineer/Specialist, ALT, eikaiwa, international-school, preschool, online, and side-teaching situations.

Add sourced qualification alternatives, duties and exclusions, periods and renewal, and a broad occupation map including software developer, software engineer, programmer, systems engineer, design, translation, language instruction, marketing, planning, sales, accounting, and consulting examples.

Make English teacher, ALT, school teacher, international-school, vocational-school, preschool, dispatch, and multiple-worksite distinctions visible while tying classification to the institution and duties.
Cover university professor, associate and assistant professor, lecturer, language instructor, researcher, and research-supervision titles without treating rank as determinative.
Cover corporate, government, institute, laboratory, R&D, and scientific-research roles and distinguish university, product-development, regulated clinical, and designated-program work.

Add prior overseas service, corporate relationship, office, transfer-period, remuneration, and covered-duty rules plus representative technical, consulting, finance, marketing, design, and language roles.
Give employers a lawful hiring, activity-fit, evidence, authorized COE support, onboarding, reporting, and change-management workflow parallel to but distinct from the education-provider guide.
Retain the route-neutral comparison and point its employer workflow and common title examples to the detailed status and employer guides.
Connect multiple teaching appointments, consulting, contracting, freelance, and cross-category activity examples without duplicating the outside-activity rules.
Keep resident and employer reporting separate and connect employment changes to route-specific status fit.
Expose organization-facing guidance only when substantive employer content exists.
Provide employers a focused sequence from role design and lawful recruitment through COE support, arrival, employment reporting, and later changes.

Index common titles and questions including English teacher, ALT, eikaiwa, international school, university lecturer, software developer, programmer, systems engineer, researcher, and company transfer.

scopeBoundaries: Iteration 5B should implement only the five academic and technical work statuses and the shared employer-facing guide; regulated and creative professions remain Iteration 6, and business and workforce programs remain Iteration 7.
Job titles are explanatory examples and search aids, never a whitelist, guarantee, or substitute for actual duties, qualifications, institution, contract, and current official criteria.
The employer guide is an operational orientation, not individualized legal advice and not a substitute for ISA, the labour authorities, a licensed attorney, or an administrative scrivener.
Nihonest must not say that an employer sponsors, issues, approves, or guarantees a COE without clarifying the precise support or representative role and ISA's decision-making authority.
Exact document inventories must link to the current application context and organization category instead of being frozen as one universal checklist.
Employment law, immigration permission, professional licensing, tax, social insurance, and contract restrictions remain separate legal layers even when one event affects several of them.

The English-teaching comparison should classify common institutional scenarios but must direct unclear international-school, preschool, tutoring, dispatch, online, freelance, and mixed-role cases to an authoritative individual check.
Iteration 5B should add an `employer` Audience value only when the employer guide and journey are available, avoiding an empty or misleading filter.
No researched guide or structured assertion becomes verified without explicit human approval under the Phase 12 editorial workflow.
unresolvedQuestions: Should dispatched ALT arrangements receive their own conditional block in Instructor, given that the employer, worksite, and contract structure may differ, or remain an edge-case callout pending stronger source detail?

How should international schools, kindergartens, preschools, cram schools, after-school programs, and online teaching platforms be labeled in public guidance when their English names do not establish their Japanese legal institution category?
Should the employer journey appear as a default Explore content group once created, or initially through the Employer audience filter and contextual links as with education-provider guidance?

Should occupation examples be stored only in structured status records and article `searchTerms`, or should a reusable occupation-to-status comparison structure be introduced now for the later Can I do this feature?
How much employment-law and social-insurance onboarding belongs in the employer guide versus links to the later Phase 13 integration and compliance curriculum?

scopeApproval.note: The editor approved the proposed scope and explicitly required the concise standalone English-teaching comparison guide.
